name: What can go wrong with a primary suite addition?

mainEntity.name: What can go wrong with a primary suite addition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The most common risks are underestimated site work, difficult utility connections, structural surprises, design changes after work begins, delayed selections, and water or ventilation problems in the bathroom. A new roof and exterior wall also create potential tie-in points where poor detailing can cause leaks or finish cracking.

These risks cannot all be eliminated, but they can be reduced through measured drawings, appropriate structural review, a detailed scope, early selections, inspections, and written change management. In the City of San Diego, construction and building-system alterations generally require permits before work starts.

Key factors:
- Existing foundation and soil conditions
- Sewer, water, electrical, and HVAC capacity
- Roof drainage and flashing details
- Bathroom waterproofing and exhaust routing

Practical guidance: Ask which conditions are verified and which remain allowances. Keep a written record of approved changes, costs, and schedule effects rather than relying on informal conversations.

Elite Remodeling & Design’s coordinated design-to-construction process is intended to connect planning details with field execution.
acceptedAnswer.description: Problems can include hidden foundation issues, difficult plumbing routes, roof leaks, insufficient HVAC capacity, delayed materials, design changes, and bathroom moisture failures. Reduce exposure with measured plans, early selections, a detailed scope, permit coordination, written change orders, and clear allowances for concealed conditions.
